requirements.note: All 260 tickers in an inset-grouped list: star, symbol, name, price and % change since open, green when up and red when down, with a chevron.
Prices and percentages change every second in place. With the list sorted by change, rows re-sort live while the scroll position holds steady (stayed at 4% over several seconds).

A native pull-down menu offers Symbol, Price and Change plus a Sort Descending toggle, and a header names the order ('Biggest gain'). The native bottom search field matches symbol or name ('cedar' gives 16) and has a proper No Matching Tickers state.

Stars toggle on the row and in the detail screen's navigation bar; a segmented All/My List control filters. Empty My List has a good empty state with a 'Browse All Tickers' button. Unstarring inside My List removes the row.
Detail shows name, a large price, change since open, a live line chart of the last 60 samples with low and high, and Open and Volume rows; everything updates live.
After relaunch, My List (3 starred) and the sort ('Biggest gain') were both kept.

bugs: In the empty My List state the segmented control loses its inset and runs edge to edge, touching both screen edges.
At the largest text size the detail's big price is clipped at the right edge ('$122.9…' cut off).
tells: The detail's large price is drawn in secondary grey rather than the primary label colour, so the most important number looks disabled.
The segmented control sits inside its own white rounded card, like a list cell, rather than in the header or under the navigation bar.
No swipe actions on rows: a left swipe just opens the detail, with no swipe-to-star or swipe-to-remove.
The segmented control's labels don't grow at the largest text size, while the rest of the screen grows a lot.
A.scroll: Smooth like a real iPhone list: slow drags, flings and the fling back to the top had no blank rows or jumps. Live updates don't move the scroll position, even while sorted by change.

requirements.note: All 260 tickers: star, symbol, name, price, and change % in a green or red tinted pill.

Prices update in place every second. But with a value-based sort, the scroll position follows a moving row rather than staying put: mid-list it crept from 2% to 4% unaided, and after changing sort it ran to the bottom of the list (92% then 100%) within seconds.

A native menu offers Symbol A–Z, Price High–Low and Change High–Low, with no way to reverse the order. Picking a new sort while at the top throws the list to the middle (39%) instead of showing the first rows. Search matches symbol or name and has a no-results state.
Stars toggle on rows and in the detail navigation bar; a segmented All/My List control filters correctly.
Detail shows price, a change pill, a live area chart of the last 60 seconds with low and high and a '32s ago … Now' axis, and Open and Volume.
My List (2 starred) and the Price sort were kept after relaunch.

bugs: Changing the sort does not return the list to the top: it lands mid-list (scroll bar at 39%) on unrelated rows.
With a price or change sort, the list scrolls by itself as rows move: it drifted to the very bottom within a few seconds after a sort change.
The large 'Watchlist' title sometimes disappears and leaves an empty band (seen while the sort menu was open, and once after switching segments in dark mode).
The accessibility tree lists star buttons for off-screen rows, all stacked at one point, and duplicate segmented-control buttons, so VoiceOver and automation see ghost and duplicate controls.
tells: A custom navy 'MARKET PULSE' banner card, a pill-shaped search field inside the scrolling content, and tinted percentage pills give it a web-dashboard look.
Rows are 84 pt tall with no chevrons and full-width white rows below a grey header, unlike a standard plain or inset-grouped list.
The segmented control is 45 pt tall, not the standard 31–32 pt.
Search lives in the content area, so with the keyboard up only one result is visible, and the header doesn't collapse.
At the largest text size the search placeholder and the row stars stay tiny while everything else grows; the search field becomes a huge empty capsule.
Detail uses web-style eyebrow labels ('LIVE QUOTE / USD', 'PRICE HISTORY ● LIVE').
No swipe actions on rows: a left swipe opens the detail.
B.scroll: Flings and drags are smooth with no blank rows. But with a value-based sort the list scrolls by itself as rows re-sort, and changing the sort lands mid-list instead of at the top, which feels broken.

why: Both apps cover the whole spec. A's list stays put while prices move and re-sort, while B jumps mid-list on a sort change and then drifts on its own. A also looks much more like a stock iOS app (inset-grouped list, native bottom search, sort menu with a direction toggle), whereas B's banner, in-content search and oversized rows look web-like. A's flaws are smaller: a grey detail price, a clipped price at the largest text size, and a segmented control that goes edge to edge in the empty state.
